title: UPDATE: Altman Says OpenAI Let AI Math Research Get 'Out of Control for One Week' Amid Backlash
summary:
OpenAI Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman admitted the company let its AI math research get "out of control for one week" following backlash from mathematicians over its mass release of solved problems. Speaking on Stripe co-founder John Collison's Cheeky Pint podcast, Altman also confirmed that OpenAI holds additional unpublished proofs beyond the more than 700 problems it already released on GitHub.

"Humanity deserves fundamental knowledge. And we should not be sitting on a major fundamental science discovery," Altman said on the podcast, while acknowledging that for a scientist, "your career and a significant amount of your enjoyment and fulfillment in life comes from discovering science." Collison compared the reaction among mathematicians—including an essay by Cornell math professor Steven Strogatz on the impact of the dump—to port automation, saying "the longshoremen union weren't happy" either.

Beyond the bulk math dump, OpenAI has drawn scrutiny from researchers over how it handled three flagship discoveries from an unreleased internal model. The company posted raw proofs and Lean verifications directly to GitHub claiming a resolution of the local smoothing and Kakeya conjectures in every dimension and a refutation of the 1999 Exponential Time Hypothesis, for which original proposers Russell Impagliazzo and Ramamohan Paturi alongside MIT's Ryan Williams have since opened a public discussion blog and paper depository. By contrast, OpenAI withheld its 1,147-page proof covering the existence of four dimensional pure Yang-Mills theory and quantum chromodynamics, deferring release to a review panel led by Nobel laureate David Gross despite demands from the Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence to make the files public.

selectedTweets.text:
The physics collaboration will understand and explain a result that gives a mathematically rigorous existence proof of certain interacting quantum field theories containing gauge fields and fermions in four dimensions, including Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) and a unified completion of the Standard Model of particle physics.

As a subproblem, this work also includes a proof of the existence of pure Yang–Mills theory, which is part of the Quantum Yang–Mills Theory Clay Mathematics Institute Millennium Prize problem. These proofs are all formally verified in Lean.

Our models produced a natural language proof for Yang–Mills existence, and then subsequently produced a proof for QCD After the formalization completed, we reached out to David Gross. David will lead a group including Michael Douglas, Arthur Jaffe, Igor Klebanov, and Nikita Nekrasov that will shepherd this work, and we will defer to them on the release of materials.

Gross’s work on asymptotic freedom in Yang-Mills theories helped establish QCD as the theory of the strong interactions and earned him a share of the 2004 Nobel Prize in Physics. Jaffe formulated the Quantum Yang–Mills Theory Millenium Prize problem with Witten and also envisioned the idea of Millennium Prize problems and co-founded the Clay Mathematics Institute. Douglas has already been a steward of this problem over the last 20 years; Klebanov helped pioneer the application of gauge–string duality to confinement, an important property of QCD, and now directs the Simons Collaboration on Confinement and QCD Strings; and Nekrasov has done groundbreaking work on exact methods for generalizations of Yang–Mills theory.

selectedTweets.text:
SITUATION EXPLAINED: OpenAI says its AI cracked 3 major open problems in math, computer science, and physics at once.

• The math result claims to prove "local smoothing" for waves in every dimension, which would settle the Kakeya, Stein restriction, and Bochner-Riesz conjectures together
• That would turn Hong Wang's 3D Kakeya proof, which won a Fields Medal this year, into a special case
• The CS result refutes the exponential time hypothesis, the belief that problems like 3-SAT always take exponential time
• Hundreds of papers rely on that assumption, and OpenAI says the proof was checked in Lean
• The physics result claims existence proofs for 4D Yang-Mills, QCD, and a grand unified theory, but not the mass gap needed for the $1M Millennium Prize
• A group led by Nobel laureate David Gross is reviewing the physics proof, and its materials haven't been released
• OpenAI says it won't seek academic credit for discoveries made by its internal models
